::: {#exr-alternating}
## The alternating harmonic series

The alternating harmonic series converges to $\ln 2$:
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k} = 1 - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} - \ldots = \ln 2.
$$

1. Implement the function `partial_sums(n)`, which returns the vector of the partial sums $s_1, \ldots, s_n$.

1. Compute the errors of $s_{10}$, $s_{100}$ and $s_{1000}$. How many terms are needed for one more correct digit? Compare with the geometric series from @exr-geometric.

::: {.lm-scaffold}
```{julia}
# function partial_sums(n)
#     ...
# end
```
:::

::: {.lm-solution}
The function is in `src/partial_sums.jl` (see the appendix).

```{julia}
sums = partial_sums(1000)
ns = [10, 100, 1000]
[ns abs.(sums[ns] .- log(2))]
```

The error is about $1 / (2n)$: one more correct digit needs ten times as many terms. The geometric series with $q = 1/10$ gains one digit with each term.
:::
:::
